items.claim: This span's back seam is argued in English: the cross-seam carry catchword is named without a Hebrew form or a tier, and a second byte-true device straddling the same seam is left undisclosed.
items.evidence: Three distinct Hebrew families cross the Isa.46.2|Isa.46.3 seam, and none is named in Hebrew. Load root: נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם and מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte), מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte), הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte), אֶשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte). Load-bearer root in a plene/defective pair: עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte) against הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte) -- the two spellings are disjoint under consonantal search (sweep: 1 verse each for the plene and the defective spelling), so the tie is root-level, not a form recurrence, a distinction the rendering 'carried' erases in both places. Entirely undisclosed is a third device: the rescue pair מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte) answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte) (sweep: 7 verses book-wide for the rescue root at skeleton tier). The span quotes both renderings of that pair ('could not deliver', 'will deliver') without registering that a byte-true device straddles its own boundary, which argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. Separately, 'the same noun recurs' at Isa.46.2 is a Hebrew recurrence claim with no quoted form and no tier: מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1) and מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2) are NOT byte-identical -- the accents differ -- and match only at accent-stripped tier. The role-split itself is correct: both sites are the burden common noun, not a verse-initial oracle header. Finally, the single-witness SAMEKH filed here as an 'interior division' is a segment terminating MT 46:2, so it falls on this span's own back seam and corroborates it; the span opening at Isa.46.3 labels the identical segment a front-seam division.

items.claim: The strongest rival cut inside the span -- a fresh vocative under the same summons formula at Isa.46.12 -- is recast as an inclusio rather than disclosed as the rival, and a weaker site is disclosed in its place.
items.evidence: The boundary logic used at this span's own front seam is 'summons formula plus fresh addressee'. Both stand at MT 46:12. The formula שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte) matches the opening שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte) at accent-stripped tier only -- the span states that tier correctly, which is good discipline -- but the vocative that follows is a DIFFERENT addressee: אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte) against בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte). A single-witness SAMEKH terminates MT 46:11, so it falls exactly on the Isa.46.11|Isa.46.12 seam and corroborates that site; the span discloses that segment only as an 'interior division' and never relates it to the reading it declines. The disclosed rival names Isa.46.8 instead, where no summons formula, no vocative and no mark stands. Two further items. The rescue pair מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte) / וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte) straddles this span's front seam undisclosed, although the span quotes the answering carry claim at Isa.46.4 as a deliberate contrast. And the SAMEKH terminating MT 46:13 is filed as an interior division here, while the span opening at Isa.47.1 calls the same segment a front-seam division. Object naming is otherwise right: שְׁאֵרִ֖ית (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte) is the sheerit noun (sweep: 4 verses book-wide for that noun), correctly kept apart from the other three objects on the same root, and the K/Q note at MT 46:11 is disclosed.

items.claim: The ground given for holding Isa.47.4 inside the span -- syntactic continuity with a surrounding sentence -- is not in the pointed text, and the digit offered in the disclosed rival names no swept object.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.47.4 is גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (byte) -- a self-contained verbless nominal clause with no verb to continue any preceding sentence. The verse before it closes נָקָ֣ם אֶקָּ֔ח וְלֹ֥א אֶפְגַּ֖ע אָדָֽם (oshb:Isa.47.3, byte) and is terminated by a single-witness SAMEKH, and the verse after opens a fresh feminine imperative pair שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי (oshb:Isa.47.5, byte). So even the weak mark layer isolates MT 47:4 rather than embedding it, and 'holds it inside the surrounding sentence' is a form claim the bytes do not carry. Second, '(sweep: 15 verses)' is offered for 'the addressee stays the same across the chapter's 15 verses', but 15 is the chapter's verse count, not a count of a swept object; the addressee-continuity object is never swept, and the span's own reading of Isa.47.4 as a first-person-plural communal aside contradicts unbroken addressee continuity. The bounds themselves stand: רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte) is a genuine feminine imperative onset; the title at MT 47:4 is a real qadosh-Israel title site (sweep: 25 title verses book-wide for the title construct, the trisagion being a separate object); and the back seam is corroborated by the SAMEKH terminating MT 47:7 -- which this span files as an 'interior division' although it sits on that boundary, where the span opening at Isa.47.8 calls the same segment a front-seam division. The paseq at MT 47:1 is correctly cited count-only with no intra-verse position claim.

items.claim: The onset at Isa.47.8 is licensed by a cross-chapter 'same summons pattern' claim that carries no tier label and matches at no tier in the Hebrew -- it holds only in the English rendering.
items.evidence: MT 47:8 opens וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי זֹ֤את (oshb:Isa.47.8, byte); the verse it is equated with opens שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte). The two are not byte-identical, not accent-stripped identical, and not identical consonantally. The feminine-singular hear-this collocation stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide and the masculine-plural hear-this collocation in exactly 2 (sweep: 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier), and the two hit sets are disjoint. No form is quoted from the verse being compared to and no tier is named, so the recurrence survives only because both renderings read 'hear this'. The comparison is load-bearing: it is what makes Isa.47.8 an onset of the same class as the front seam of the span opening at Isa.48.1. The second site of the plural collocation is MT 48:16, which no span in this review set quotes at all. The remainder is clean: the K/Q note at MT 47:13 is disclosed with the accurate statement that the span does not quote through it, and the SAMEKH terminating MT 47:15 is disclosed -- though as an 'interior division' when it in fact falls on this span's own back seam, where the span opening at Isa.48.1 calls the same segment a front-seam division.

items.claim: Both bounds are carried by the pointed bytes, the title object inside the span is byte-backed, and every single-witness layer owed by the span is disclosed.
items.evidence: The front seam is a genuine tier-1 onset: שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את בֵּֽית יַעֲקֹ֗ב (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte) is a plural summons with a fresh vocative, corroborated by the single-witness SAMEKH terminating MT 47:15 -- which this span identifies correctly as a front-seam division. The back seam at Isa.48.11|Isa.48.12 is corroborated by the SAMEKH terminating MT 48:11 and by a real form-class change in the bytes: שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.48.12, byte) is singular against this span's plural שִׁמְעוּ (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte); both witnesses' renderings are consistent with that change and neither contradicts it. The of-hosts title signal is byte-backed inside the span: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.48.2, byte). Disclosure is complete for the span: both parashah segments (MT 48:2, MT 48:11) and the paseq at MT 48:1 are cited as single-witness with no intra-verse position claim, and there is no K/Q note anywhere in MT ch 48, so nothing is owed there. One wrinkle, not enough to unseat the span: the segment terminating MT 48:11 is filed as an 'interior division' although it sits on this span's own back seam, and the span opening at Isa.48.12 labels the identical segment a front-seam division.

items.claim: The span declines a rival cut at Isa.48.16 without ever putting the rival's byte evidence on the page, and that evidence is the strongest form recurrence anywhere in this review set.
items.evidence: MT 48:16 opens with a plural imperative pair the span never quotes: קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֗את (oshb:Isa.48.16, byte). Its hear-this collocation is ACCENT-STRIPPED IDENTICAL to שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte), and consonantal search puts that collocation in exactly 2 verses book-wide -- MT 48:1 and MT 48:16 and nowhere else (sweep: 2 verses). What the span does quote from that verse is only its closing half, וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.48.16, byte). The other declined rival is likewise unquoted: MT 48:14 opens הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.48.14, byte), an assemble-and-hear imperative pair. A seam claim resting on a frame -- including a claim that a frame does NOT open a unit -- has to show the form. The mark layer would in fact have helped here and is not used: the PE at MT 48:16 is a segment terminating that verse, so it divides Isa.48.16|Isa.48.17 and does not corroborate an onset AT Isa.48.16; the span files it only as an 'interior division' while arguing precisely about whether that verse opens a unit. Credit where due: the koh-amar engagement is correct -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.48.17, byte) is quoted, its owner is named as the divine frame, and MT 48:17 is a divine-frame site, not one of the four royal-messenger sites; the qadosh-Israel signal is byte-backed at that same verse; and the first-person voice at Isa.48.16 is properly held rather than assigned.

items.claim: The stated seam ground -- a bare imperative 'with no hear-formula' -- is contradicted by the span's own opening verse, where a hear-root imperative with the same object stands in the bytes.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.48.20 carries הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את (byte): a causative plural imperative on the hear root with the identical object that the seams at MT 47:8, MT 48:1 and MT 48:16 are argued from. Consonantal search finds that causative collocation in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse), so it is not a formula recurrence -- but that is a ROLE distinction, proclamation directed outward versus a summons to the addressee, and the span makes no such distinction: it asserts the absence of a hear-formula flatly, a statement that survives only because the rendering it quotes reads 'announce this' and hides the root. High confidence is then assigned to a bound resting on that statement. The rest is handled well and should be preserved: צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte) is correctly read as a departure-imperative onset; גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte) is correctly kept apart from the unnamed servant-figure zones, since the referent is named in the verse's own bytes; and the closing-verdict pair is described exactly right -- אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.48.22, byte) against אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י (oshb:Isa.57.21, byte), with אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם and לָרְשָׁעִֽים byte-identical on both sides including accents -- although that recurrence claim itself carries no tier label and quotes no form from the second site. The SAMEKH terminating MT 48:22 is again filed as 'interior' where it closes the span; the span opening at Isa.49.1 names the same segment as standing ahead of its own opening.

items.claim: Both seam grounds are asserted without the bytes: the back bound rests on an unquoted, unattributed frame at Isa.49.7, and the front-seam contrast mischaracterises the material it contrasts with.
items.evidence: The back bound is argued from 'the fresh messenger-formula frame' at Isa.49.7 with no form quoted and no frame owner named. The bytes: MT 49:7 opens כֹּ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָה֩ גֹּאֵ֨ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte) -- a DIVINE frame, not one of the four royal-messenger sites -- and the same verse carries the defective title spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte) beside the distinct suffixed epithet קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte): two separate objects that a citation of that verse as seam evidence should not pass over. At the front, the span contrasts its first-person opening with 'the third-person restoration material immediately before it' and supplies no text reference for that material at all. The bytes contradict the characterisation: the immediately preceding verses are second-person plural address -- צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ and הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte) -- closing on a divine speech signature, אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.48.22, byte). Third, both K/Q verses in the span are disclosed generically as K/Q-bearing, but the pointed splices run straight through the doubled token pairs -- לא ל֣וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.5, byte) and ונצירי וּנְצוּרֵ֥י (oshb:Isa.49.6, byte) -- without naming which form the run engages, and each run is labelled a single byte tier although the unpointed ketiv tokens inside it are skeleton-grade and are not labelled as such. What the span gets right is the hardest part: all six splices reach byte tier; the mark and paseq disclosures are complete and, uniquely in this set, correctly placed (the SAMEKH terminating MT 49:6 is named as closing the span, the SAMEKH terminating MT 48:22 as standing ahead of the opening, the paseq at MT 49:5 count-only); and the referent tension between עַבְדִּי אָ֑תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֕ל (oshb:Isa.49.3, byte) and the commissioning at Isa.49.5-Isa.49.6 is named and left undecided.
